title: The Monsoon of Cape Reckoning
premise: Freya Hartwell, a bush pilot ferrying medicine and gossip across the rain-soaked interior of Cape Reckoning, is hired to search for a vanished government survey team. She finds their camp stripped clean and a tide chart marking a wreck that shouldn't exist—a colonial-era ship her own grandfather's logs hint he once found and hid. Racing a salvage fleet that arrives in six tides, Freya must decide whether to protect the family secret that kept her community invisible, or reveal the truth the wilderness has been keeping. In the end she chooses truth over inheritance, guiding the fleet to the wreck but not before recovering the one artifact—her grandfather's confession—that rewrites who her family really was.
about_author: Coral Sandoval spent a decade flying supply runs along remote coastlines before turning to fiction, drawing on the pilots, salvagers, and stubborn townsfolk she met there. She writes adventure stories about people whose loyalties are tested by landscapes that keep no secrets and forgive no mistakes.

chapters.title: Weather Coming In
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A routine medicine run into the interior establishes her world: the airstrip at Cape Reckoning, the townsfolk who depend on her, and the monsoon season closing in. She overhears rumors of a government survey team gone quiet. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath competent calm.

chapters.title: The Contract
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. A government liaison offers her double rates to fly a search grid for the missing survey team, warning her off certain coordinates. Her mechanic and closest friend, Tomas, urges her to refuse. Emotional beat: the pull of easy money against instinct that something is being hidden from her.

chapters.title: First Grid
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, airborne. Flying the official search pattern through worsening weather, she spots nothing—until a glint outside the sanctioned grid catches her eye. She logs it privately. Emotional beat: the first crack between loyalty to her employers and loyalty to her own judgment.

chapters.title: What the Camp Kept
chapters.summary: Freya and Tomas hike to the glint site and find the survey camp: gear intact, food untouched, no tracks leading out. A tide chart pinned inside a tent marks six dates and a hand-drawn coastline that matches nowhere official. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Logbook
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, night. Back home she digs out her late grandfather's pilot logbooks and finds gaps—flights never filed, coordinates smudged by his own hand. The drawn coastline matches one of them. Emotional beat: the discovery that her inheritance includes deliberate silence.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A salvage company's advance ship docks at Cape Reckoning, buying goodwill with cash and questions. Its captain, Ilse Varga, interviews locals about the survey team—and about old Hartwell flights. Emotional beat: the town's loyalty beginning to be bought, and Tomas feeling it slip.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Working the tide chart against nautical almanacs, she calculates the wreck will surface—or become reachable—at the sixth high tide, four days out. Varga makes her an offer to join the salvage as pilot. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Old Woman of the Point
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She visits Maren, the last person who flew with her grandfather, now elderly and sharp-tongued. Maren confirms the wreck exists and warns: 'He hid it so no one would have to choose what you're choosing.' Emotional beat: grief for a grandfather she thought she knew.

chapters.title: Burned Chart
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Someone ransacks Freya's hangar; her copied chart is stolen, though the original logbook survives hidden in the plane. Suspicion falls on a dockhand in Varga's pay. Emotional beat: the race turns personal; invisibility is officially over.

chapters.title: Storm Grounding
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The monsoon grounds all flights for a day, trapping everyone ashore while Varga's fleet repositions. Freya and Varga share a tense dinner where each probes the other's motives. Emotional beat: grudging respect between adversaries who recognize themselves in each other.

chapters.title: The Survey Team's Last Flight
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Reconstructing the survey team's route, she realizes they didn't vanish—they were running from something, heading inland toward the wreck's coordinates on foot. She finds a dropped field notebook describing 'the hold' and 'the manifest.' Emotional beat: hope that the team may still be alive.

chapters.title: Inland
chapters.summary: Freya and Tomas trek upriver following the notebook, weather deteriorating. They find a survivor's lean-to, days cold, and fresh footprints heading toward the coast caves. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into urgency—they are close behind someone living.

chapters.title: The Caves at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At low tide they enter sea caves below the point and find two surviving survey members, injured and hiding—not from the wilderness, but from Varga's people, whom they'd discovered were falsifying heritage surveys to claim the wreck. Emotional beat: betrayal reframes everything; the government was never the real threat.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Reckoning
chapters.summary: Survivor Amara's POV. The survivors explain: the wreck is the Reckoning, a colonial ship carrying seized artifacts from the region's Indigenous trade networks—and documents proving the cargo was never lawfully claimed. Varga's fleet wants it erased or owned. Emotional beat: the weight of history made physical.

chapters.title: Tide Four
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. With two tides left, the fleet anchors offshore. Freya flies a decoy run to draw their spotter planes east while Tomas moves the survivors to safety. Emotional beat: loyalty to the town now means deceiving the law that pays her.

chapters.title: Varga's Bargain
chapters.summary: Varga's POV. Confronted by Freya, Varga reveals she knows about the Hartwell logbook and offers a partnership: split the find, bury the manifest, make Freya's family rich and safe. Emotional beat: the offer aimed precisely at Freya's oldest wound—invisibility as protection.

chapters.title: What Grandfather Chose
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, night before the fifth tide. Reading the final pages of the logbook, she finds her grandfather's confession: he hid the wreck not to protect treasure, but because revealing it would have destroyed the coastal communities' land claims. He chose silence out of love. Emotional beat: understanding, then refusal—love doesn't require lies anymore.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Freya and Tomas's alternating POV. The wreck's mast breaks the surface at low tide; both fleets converge. Freya lands on the exposed sandbar and recovers the sealed manifest case just as Varga's crew storms the bar. Emotional beat: pure adrenaline, every theme colliding in the surf.

chapters.title: The Stand on the Sandbar
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Cornered by Varga, Freya broadcasts the manifest's contents over open radio—every frequency, the whole coast listening—including proof of the fraudulent surveys. Varga's own crew hesitates; the fleet's legal cover evaporates mid-theft. Emotional beat: truth deployed as a weapon, costly and liberating.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Freya and Tomas's POV. The sixth tide surges in faster than forecast; the sandbar begins to drown with Freya, Tomas, and the case still aboard the damaged plane. A desperate takeoff through spray and crosswind. Emotional beat: the wilderness forgiving nothing, and nearly collecting.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She crash-lands on the strip at Cape Reckoning, alive, the manifest intact. Officials arrest Varga's officers; the survey survivors testify; the artifacts' custody passes to the region's descendant communities. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by cost—the town knows everything now, including her family's lie.

chapters.title: Clear Air After Rain
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, epilogue. Weeks later, she files her grandfather's logbook with the archive, ending the family's inherited silence, and takes Amara up for her first flight over the recovered wreck site. The monsoon breaks; the air is clean. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed—from secrets kept to truths carried forward.
